articles.title: Neural Defend ARCAS 290M: A Robust Foundation Model for AI-Generated Audio Detection
articles.summary: Voice cloning now needs only seconds of audio, and detectors tuned to one dataset often fail when the generator, channel, or language changes. We introduce ARCAS 290M, Neural Defend's foundation model for detecting AI-generated audio. A single frozen production model, with no benchmark-specific fine-tuning, generalizes across text-to-speech, voice-conversion, and codec-language-model generators, telephone and Bluetooth channels, recording conditions, and languages. We evaluate it on the complete official test sets of ten public benchmarks, scoring every recording exactly as released, and against commercial systems on independent leaderboards. ARCAS 290M ranks first among all systems on the Podonos leaderboard and has the lowest equal error rate among commercial detectors on ASVspoof5. It separates real from AI-generated speech almost perfectly on ASVspoof5, SpeechFake, and ShiftySpeech, and detects nearly all AI-generated speech in Hindi, Tamil, Bengali, and Telugu. On every benchmark with a published zero-shot comparison, including in-the-wild audio, partial fakes, and the conditions hardest for the field, it surpasses the strongest reported detector by a wide margin. These results establish ARCAS 290M as a general-purpose foundation for AI-generated audio detection in fraud prevention, platform safety, and media verification.

articles.title: SKILL.PNG: Learning Agent Skills in Pixel Space
articles.summary: AI agents are commonly specialized for new tasks and domains using skills, i.e. natural language instructions placed in their context. However, the discrete nature of textual skills prevents continuous optimization. Gradient-based approaches such as finetuning, on the other hand, are typically model-specific, preventing skill transfer across different agents. Since many agents today are built on vision-language models (VLMs), we can address these limitations by introducing Skill$.$png: a method for obtaining skill-like image inputs whose pixels are optimized with gradient descent through the vision encoder of a frozen VLM. Image skills are compatible with any VLM, and a single image can be optimized jointly for an ensemble of models. We show that Skill$.$png significantly outperforms state-of-the-art textual skills optimized using frontier LLMs in 9 of 16 settings (across 4 VLMs and 4 benchmarks) while requiring only 64 to 256 image tokens instead of roughly 900 to 2000 text tokens at inference time. Hybrid skills, i.e. text and image skills jointly optimized, further improve agent performance. Moreover, an image optimized with an ensemble of VLMs can successfully transfer across the models in the ensemble. Skill$.$png thus presents the first agent skill that can be optimized with gradient descent while retaining transfer benefits of text skills. Our code is available at: https://github.com/omseeth/skill.png

articles.title: Highly Efficient Vertical Federated Clustering with Triangle-Inequality-based Pruning
articles.summary: In many real-world scenarios, multiple parties hold complementary feature subsets for the same samples but cannot share raw data. This makes efficient clustering over distributed feature subsets an important and challenging problem. While vertical federated learning (VFL) enables such collaboration, existing VFL clustering methods often require many communication rounds or substantial local computation. To address these limitations, we first propose TriCD, an exact pruning method for CDKM that preserves the same cluster assignments under the same initialization. TriCD constructs triangle-inequality bounds on demand to skip redundant objective evaluations with negligible extra space. Building upon this, we propose FedTriCD, an efficient federated clustering algorithm. By decomposing the global objective into client-local subproblems, FedTriCD enables pruning-based local optimization using only local data. FedTriCD further reduces communication by allowing multiple local updates between server synchronizations. A proximal regularization term is introduced to control the drift caused by infrequent communication. Our theoretical analysis establishes the exactness and finite convergence of TriCD and provides a bounded-error server-side update guarantee for FedTriCD. Experiments on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate the efficiency and clustering quality of the proposed methods. TriCD achieves up to a 50.07$\times$ speedup over \Lloyd's algorithm. Moreover, FedTriCD achieves competitive clustering quality while requiring fewer local evaluations and fewer communication rounds than state-of-the-art federated clustering methods.

articles.title: Windchime: an Audiovisual Installation with Audio-Language Model implementations
articles.summary: Windchime is an audiovisual installation in which spoken language retrieves music and interactive animations from an artist authored corpus. A local Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) model transcribes each prompt while an audio-language model (ALM) embeds it and retrieval over 406 audio stems returns a soundscape with live coded Strudel fragments that layer into audio output. Simultaneously each spoken input results in retrieval of interactive Three.js animation scenes each containing unique tactile control via monome grid and arc hardware. Windchime distributes agency in three distinct directions; across the artist who authored the possible outputs, the ALM that influences what areas of the corpus can be retrieved, and the visitor whose spoken inputs result in multimodal embodied interaction.

articles.title: Disentangling Self-Distillation: Measuring and Modeling Acquisition and Retention
articles.summary: Self-distillation with privileged context adapts a language model from demonstrations by letting the model, once conditioned on a reference response, teach its context-free copy token by token. Our taxonomy reveals existing methods differ along three entangled axes: (i) the rollout source (student or teacher), (ii) the teacher coupling (frozen, or an exponential moving average of the student at some coupling rate) and (iii) the token-level divergence (here, reverse or forward KL), yet these axes are usually studied in fixed combinations and have led to conflicting conclusions. We formalize a unifying framework that covers both self-distillation and classic supervised fine-tuning: we train every combination of the three axes, on Qwen2.5-7B and Ministral-3-3B across ordinary and contradictory tasks, totaling 1,200 adaptation runs, to systematically investigate the impact of the above axes. We propose a controlled model of the same objective to interpret the resulting acquisition-retention trade-offs. We find that (i) the rollout source matters mostly where the task contradicts the pretrained behavior: there teacher rollouts raise acquisition (the accuracy gained on the new task) well above what student rollouts achieve, with almost no change in retention (the change in accuracy on general benchmarks); (ii) the teacher coupling changes acquisition most, on every task: acquisition rises with the coupling rate, then falls past a task-specific rate; (iii) switching the KL direction costs retention in one model but not the other, so which axis to tune first depends on the model. The controlled model reproduces the three trends.

articles.title: Self-Distilled Reasoner: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Language Models
articles.summary: Knowledge distillation improves large language model (LLM) reasoning by compressing the knowledge of a teacher LLM to train smaller LLMs. On-policy distillation advances this approach by having the student sample its own trajectories while a teacher LLM provides dense token-level supervision, addressing the distribution mismatch between training and inference in off-policy distillation methods. However, on-policy distillation typically requires a separate, often larger, teacher LLM and does not explicitly leverage ground-truth solutions available in reasoning datasets. Inspired by the intuition that a sufficiently capable LLM can rationalize external privileged reasoning traces and teach its weaker self, we introduce On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), a learning algorithm where a single LLM acts as both teacher and student with different contexts. The teacher policy conditions on privileged information (e.g., verified reasoning traces) while the student policy sees only the question; training minimizes the per-token divergence between these distributions over the student's own rollouts. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method on multiple mathematical reasoning benchmarks, achieving superior token efficiency compared to reinforcement learning methods and better performance over off-policy distillation methods. Code repo: https://github.com/siyan-zhao/OPSD.

articles.title: Let the Gate Decide: Per-Lookup Precision for Quantized Conditional Memory in LLMs
articles.summary: Conditional memory layers, such as DeepSeek's Engram, attach large hashed n-gram tables to a language model, and removing them from DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash costs 36.8 PopQA points. Low-bit quantization loses long-tail facts first, and the standard remedy, giving more bits to frequently accessed rows, backfires: refining lookups by access frequency is worse than refining them at random. We trace this to the gate that scales each retrieved row. A lookup's quantization error is weighted by its gate, which is small for frequent n-grams, large for the rare n-grams of long-tail entities, and computable from a 1-bit code. GateRQ therefore stores each row as a ladder of 1-bit residual codes, keeps level 1 in GPU memory to compute the gate, and reads deeper levels only for the lookups the gate ranks highest. Without retraining, GateRQ cuts GPU table memory by 7.8x on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, which raises vLLM throughput by 11%-31% over FP8 tables, while losing about 1 PopQA point at 1.50 bits read per lookup and 0.2 points at 2.10 bits across two models.

articles.title: Neurodegenerative Differential Diagnosis with Knowledge-enhanced Structural Reasoning
articles.summary: Accurate differential diagnosis of neurodegenerative disorders remains challenging due to overlapping clinical manifestations and heterogeneous, often incomplete multimodal observations. Existing multimodal models can integrate imaging and clinical measurements but often overlook disease-specific evidence patterns and pairwise relations among competing diagnoses. We therefore propose Knowledge-enhanced Structural Reasoning (KnowSR), which aligns multimodal patient representations with a literature-grounded knowledge bank of disease prototypes, signed evidence directions, and pairwise diagnostic relations. Specifically, in KnowSR, patient-specific knowledge alignment and target-aware pooling inject structured disease evidence, while anchored relational reasoning reconciles pairwise diagnostic margins over a sparse differential graph, thereby collectively enhancing differential diagnostic capability. Across extensive experiments, KnowSR consistently outperforms 19 baselines on patient-level six-class diagnosis under patient-disjoint five-fold evaluation. This shows that grounding patient evidence in structured medical knowledge enables more effective differential diagnosis than naive multimodal fusion alone.

articles.title: A Detailed Survey of Machine Learning Interpretability through Feature Interactions and Additive Models
articles.summary: Interpretability has gained an immense amount of popularity over the past decade, mostly riding the wake of neural networks’ impact on the field of machine learning. The growth in success and application of neural networks, as well as other blackbox machine learning approaches, in everyday life has led to a revitalized interest in understanding the blackbox models making those decisions. In this survey, we give a holistic coverage of the current state of the interpretability literature, focusing on a detailed coverage only for machine learning tasks and feature interaction methods like SHAP explanations, functional ANOVA, and the generalized additive model. We achieve this by first mapping out the many different subareas and paradigms under the larger umbrella of the Interpretability or XAI literature. We next isolate the scope of this survey and provide a detailed account of historical developments leading to the modern convergence of interpretability through feature interactions and interpretability through additive models. Finally, we conclude with a discussion of specific domains of application and with future directions for interpretability.

articles.title: GAAMA: Graph Augmented Associative Memory for Agents
articles.summary: AI agents that talk with users across many sessions need long-term memory to stay coherent and personalized. Existing approaches use either flat retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) that ignores how memories connect, or entity-centric knowledge graphs. Entity-centric graphs split each message into separate triples, which loses its context, and in conversations the speakers become hubs linked to almost every message, so propagation through them tells retrieval little. We present GAAMA, a graph-augmented associative memory that organizes conversations around topics. It keeps verbatim episodes, uses an LLM to distill them into atomic facts and topic concepts, and then synthesizes higher-order reflections. These four node types are linked by five kinds of structural edges, and topic concepts supply the cross-cutting paths, so mega-hubs do not form. Retrieval blends nearest-neighbor similarity search with Personalized PageRank whose transitions depend on edge type. We also introduce GRAFT (Graph Repair by Augmenting Facts & Topology), an offline repair step: for questions whose retrieved evidence fell short, a bounded ReAct agent searches memory again and records the grounded answer as a fresh fact, so later questions find it directly without extra query-time cost. On LoCoMo10, GAAMA achieves the highest average score of all compared methods (79.1%) and is competitive in every question category; GRAFT adds a small further gain. In a controlled comparison, replacing GAAMA's concept-linked facts with entity relation triples lowers reward by 3.0 pp. On MemoryArena, scored on what memory alone determines, GAAMA has the best score on average.

articles.title: TopoPilot: Reliable Conversational Workflow Automation for Topological Data Analysis and Visualization
articles.summary: Recent agentic systems demonstrate that large language models can generate complex codebases from natural language prompts. Despite this progress, they present reliability concerns for scientific visualization due to invalid operations, subtle errors, and failure to resolve underspecified inputs. In this work, we introduce TopoPilot, a reliable and extensible agentic framework for automating complex scientific visualization workflows. We focus on topological data analysis and visualization as a primary use case, while designing the framework to generalize to broader visualization domains. TopoPilot employs a two-agent architecture: an orchestrator translates user prompts into workflows composed of atomic backend actions, while a verifier evaluates workflows prior to execution. Its modular design isolates components and supports new topological descriptors and domain-specific workflows without modifying the core system. It also employs numerous deterministic guardrails to ensure semantic consistency and accurate execution. To systematically improve reliability, we develop a taxonomy of failure modes and employ targeted safeguards for each class of error. Across 2,000 simulated multi-turn conversations spanning 100 prompts, including adversarial and infeasible requests, TopoPilot achieves a success rate exceeding 95%, compared with under 50% for a baseline without comprehensive guardrails and verification. We also show that TopoPilot outperforms Claude Code and Codex on similar prompts in terms of accuracy, completion time, and token usage.

articles.title: UA-Depth: Uncertainty-Aware Depth Restoration for Material-Agnostic Object Manipulation
articles.summary: Robotic manipulation requires accurate metric depth, yet commodity RGB-D cameras often fail on non-Lambertian objects such as transparent, reflective, and translucent materials, producing holes, structured noise, and biased depth. Most restoration methods produce only a single depth map, treating noisy and reliable regions uniformly for downstream tasks while ignoring regional uncertainty. We present UA-Depth, an uncertainty-aware depth restoration framework that iteratively co-refines depth and pixel-wise uncertainty, and uses uncertainty-gated features to suppress unreliable cues for stable updates. To strengthen zero-shot behavior, UA-Depth leverages a frozen depth foundation model as a prior to initialize missing or unreliable depth, and applies two-stage MAD-weighted log-depth scale normalization to reduce outlier bias in relative-to-metric alignment. We introduce an eight-dataset zero-shot benchmark across diverse scenes, materials, and sensors. Across these benchmarks, UA-Depth achieves the best mean rank among representative baselines, with particularly strong gains on datasets dominated by transparent and reflective objects. Beyond depth metrics, we demonstrate downstream improvements in category-level 6D pose estimation and 6D grasp synthesis by exploiting the predicted uncertainty. \emph{Code, models, and data for training and evaluation will be released upon publication.}

articles.title: Towards Clinically Interpretable Ophthalmic VQA via Spatially-Grounded Lesion Evidence
articles.summary: Visual Question Answering (VQA) holds great promise for clinical support, particularly in ophthalmology, where retinal fundus photography is essential for diagnosis. However, ophthalmic VQA benchmarks primarily emphasize answer accuracy, neglecting the explicit visual evidence necessary for clinical interpretability. In this work, we introduce FundusGround, a new benchmark for clinically interpretable ophthalmic VQA with spatially-grounded lesion evidence. Specifically, we propose a three-stage pipeline that collects 10,719 fundus images with 15,595 image-level meticulously annotated lesions. To ensure anatomical consistency and clinical validity, all lesions are spatially localized using the Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) grid, enabling standardized mapping to nine clinically meaningful retinal regions. Built upon this structured lesion evidence, 72,706 questions are then generated spanning four formats: open-ended, closed-ended, single-choice, and multiple-choice. We further benchmark multiple general- and medical- large vision-language models using dual metrics for answer accuracy and lesion-level reasoning. The experiments demonstrate that incorporating lesion-level visual evidence consistently improves model performance and transparency, highlighting the necessity of explicit spatial grounding for reliable and explainable ophthalmic VQA.

articles.title: Adaptive Lipschitz-Free Proximal Gradient Methods for Stochastic Composite Nonconvex Optimization
articles.summary: We propose {\sf ALFPG}, an Adaptive Lipschitz-Free Proximal Gradient framework for stochastic composite nonconvex minimization. It adapts stepsizes from the optimization trajectory without requiring smoothness constants or line search. For finite-sum problems, {\sf ALFPG-FS} combines coordinate-wise stepsizes, Nesterov extrapolation, and a SPIDER estimator; {\sf ALFPG-D} is its full-batch specialization. Under component-wise smoothness, bounded sublevel sets, and separate lower bounds on $f$ and $h$, {\sf ALFPG-FS} achieves expected $\epsilon$-stationarity with $\mathcal O(N+\sqrt N \epsilon^{-2})$ component-gradient evaluations. For expectation problems, we develop {\sf ALFPG-MVR1} and {\sf ALFPG-MVR2} (MVR: Momentum-based Variance Reduction). Both use one fresh sample per iteration. MVR1 uses one stochastic-gradient evaluation; MVR2 uses at most two evaluations at different points with the same sample. MVR1 requires smoothness of the expected loss; MVR2 additionally requires uniformly smooth sample losses. When the regularizer is convex or Lipschitz continuous on its effective domain and stochastic gradients are almost surely bounded, both methods achieve expected $\epsilon$-stationarity using $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\sigma^2\epsilon^{-4}+\epsilon^{-2})$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\sigma\epsilon^{-3}+\epsilon^{-2})$ stochastic-gradient evaluations, respectively. Here, $N$ is the number of component functions, $\sigma^2$ bounds the gradient noise variance, and $\widetilde{\mathcal O}$ hides polylogarithmic factors. Neither expectation variant requires prior knowledge of $\sigma$, and both recover $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ complexity in the zero-noise regime. Numerical experiments on sparse phase retrieval, linear eigenvalue problems, and neural network regression show that all four ALFPG variants generally outperform state-of-the-art proximal-gradient baselines.

articles.title: Crossing the Validation Crisis: Cross-Validation Reduces Benchmarking Variance Surprisingly Well
articles.summary: Modern machine learning progresses through empirical work, benchmarking new methods to evaluate relative performance. However, the statistical variability inherent in evaluation, exacerbated by the stochastic nature of many algorithms, often makes performance estimation unreliable with the limited test samples available. The result is a validation crisis, in which genuine advances are difficult to discern. Here, we show that doing more cross-validation markedly improves confidence when evaluating and comparing learning algorithm performances. We introduce the concept of sample gain, which quantifies the virtual data augmentation achieved by using multiple cross-validation splits to reduce benchmarking variance. Experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets (histopathologic scans and NLP fine-tuning) demonstrate that multiple splits can substantially improve the reliability and stability of performance estimates, with diminishing returns often setting in later than expected. We also introduce a procedure to dynamically early-stop cross-validation by estimating from the first few splits whether further splits will bring large sample gains. Our findings highlight the value of pushing cross-validation on available samples to achieve robust and reliable benchmarking, and lead to a simple recommendation: split repeatedly.

articles.title: Tracking and Limiting Unsupported Claim Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: A Provenance-Aware Framework
articles.summary: This research examines how unsupported claims change as they move through multi-agent pipelines. It also examines whether preserving provenance can reduce these changes. We test both homogeneous and heterogeneous pipelines. Homogeneous pipelines use the same model across agents, while heterogeneous pipelines use different models. We compare the baseline with a provenance-aware framework. The framework passes each claim with its support status, source, evidence and transmission history. No new evidence is introduced during transmission. We measure changes in claim meaning, unsupported detail accretion, semantic drift, and provenance preservation. These metrics show whether the framework limits unsupported changes as claims pass between agents.

articles.title: Proactive Defense Benchmark against Deepfake Generation
articles.summary: Despite the proliferation of proactive defenses against deepfakes, the lack of a unified evaluation protocol precludes fair comparison and masks critical vulnerabilities. To bridge this gap, we present the first comprehensive benchmark that systematically assesses disruption, robustness, and transferability encompassing pixel, perceptual, and identity metrics. Our extensive analysis reveals that fidelity and identity metrics capture orthogonal performance axes, often leading to conflicting interpretations when relied upon individually. Furthermore, we identify a fundamental trade-off where peak white-box performance signals overfitting, and we introduce a calibrated evaluation to correct generator-induced identity bias. By exposing these blind spots, we establish a rigorous standard to guide the development of genuinely generalizable protections. Project page is available at: https://proactivedefensebenchmark.github.io/

articles.title: A Deformable Attention-Based Detection Transformer with Cross-Scale Feature Fusion for Industrial Coil Spring Inspection
articles.summary: Automated visual inspection of locomotive coil springs presents significant challenges due to the morphological diversity of surface defects, substantial scale variations, and complex industrial backgrounds. This paper proposes MSD-DETR (Multi-Scale Deformable Detection Transformer), a novel detection framework that addresses these challenges through three key innovations: (1) a structural re-parameterization strategy that decouples training-time multi-branch topology from inference-time efficiency, enhancing feature extraction while maintaining real-time performance; (2) a deformable attention mechanism that enables content-adaptive spatial sampling, allowing dynamic focus on defect-relevant regions regardless of morphological irregularity; and (3) a cross-scale feature fusion architecture incorporating GSConv modules and VoVGSCSP blocks for effective multi-resolution information aggregation. Comprehensive experiments on a real-world locomotive coil spring dataset demonstrate that MSD-DETR achieves 92.4\% mAP@0.5 at 98 FPS, outperforming state-of-the-art detectors including YOLOv8 (+3.1\% mAP) and the baseline RT-DETR (+2.8\% mAP) while maintaining comparable inference speed, establishing a new benchmark for industrial coil spring quality inspection.

articles.title: Digital Foundry 称《GTA6》即便高端 PC 也难稳 60 帧，其核心瓶颈要如何解决？
articles.summary: 据Digital Foundry（数毛社）的技术分析报道，《GTA6》在PS5、XSX|S乃至PS5 Pro全部主机平台均以30帧为目标运行，在当下大量开放世界普遍提供40/60帧选项的环境下，这一结果让不少玩家感到遗憾。数毛社经过实测拆解，指出这套锁帧设定背后，是游戏庞大世界模拟带来的硬性技术门槛。 真正拖垮帧率的并非画面渲染，而是CPU的运算负担。游戏内海量NPC拥有完整日常AI，一旦发生犯罪事件，人群恐慌逃窜、警方出动、爆炸载具损毁，会瞬…

articles.title: Tracing Subliminal Learning Through Pretraining
articles.summary: Large language models trained on data generated by other models can sometimes inherit traits unrelated to that data, a phenomenon called subliminal learning. We study this phenomenon under both hard-label distillation, where students train on numbers generated by a biased teacher, and on-policy soft-label distillation, where students generate the data and the teacher's logits provide the learning signal. Using Pythia, PolyPythia, and DataDecide OLMo models, we find that transfer persists in both settings across differences in weight initialization, pretraining data order, pretraining corpus, model size, and architecture, showing that none of these shared properties is necessary for transfer. Across pretraining checkpoints, the ability to transmit a preference and the ability to acquire one develop separately: some checkpoints are more effective teachers but weaker students, and vice versa. Consistent with this distinction, cross-model transfer can be strongly asymmetric in magnitude when teacher and student roles are reversed. To investigate what carries the preference signal, we construct synthetic number sequences that match the teacher's generated number frequencies but have no dependence on the prompt or preceding numbers and find that these still induce substantial transfer in the hard-label setting. In top-$K$ soft-label distillation, removing animal tokens from the loss reduces transfer, although not completely in the same-model setting. In our experiments, soft label distillation produces more consistent transfer with less extensive training than hard label distillation. The growing use of on-policy distillation in model post-training makes this a particularly relevant setting for assessing unintended preference transfer.

articles.title: Massive Activations in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models: Pre-Attention Spikes and Inter-Spike Plateaus
articles.summary: We present the first systematic study of massive activations (MAs) in layer-interleaved Hybrid linear attention large language models (HLA LLMs), examining their architectural organization, training-time emergence, underlying mechanisms, and functional significance. Across five linear attention architectures, six hybridization configurations, and five input domains, we identify two architecture-aligned morphologies: pre-attention spikes (PAS) immediately before full attention and inter-spike plateaus (ISP) persisting through intervening linear attention layers. Denser full attention increasingly connects PAS through ISP, approaching the persistent MAs of conventional Transformers. This organization also recurs across 12 public checkpoints spanning 1.2B-397B parameters, covering linear attention and state-space hybrids. Controlled pretraining of Gated DeltaNet (GDN) hybrids up to 1.3B reveals early emergence and consolidation of both morphologies, alongside asymmetric gating effects. Specifically, full attention output gates strongly attenuate MA magnitudes without eliminating their organization, whereas removing GDN output gates yields modest amplification. Mechanistically, we develop a shared systematic-outlier account: PAS follows a localized write-sink-cancel process, while ISP is consistent with delayed cancellation. Functionally, our interventions show that deleting only the four largest-magnitude PAS coordinates at each full attention input reduces mean downstream accuracy by 21.9%-63.6% relative to normal inference. Moreover, reference-conditioned spike-to-plateau connection consistently improves mean real-world retrieval accuracy, yielding relative gains of 1.1%-12.6% without retraining. Our code is available at https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/Massive-Activations-HLA.

articles.title: DRA-HTR: Disentangling Representation and Adaptation for Handwritten Text Recognition
articles.summary: Handwritten text recognition (HTR), particularly when applied to historical documents, remains challenging due to the scarcity of annotated data and the substantial domain shifts caused by variations in handwriting styles, document degradation, acquisition conditions, and linguistic characteristics. While large amounts of unlabeled target-domain data are often available, effectively exploiting them requires adaptation strategies tailored to the specific requirements of HTR. We propose DRA-HTR, an unsupervised generative domain adaptation pipeline specifically designed for HTR and built upon the DRANet framework. The proposed approach combines source-domain pretraining, unsupervised adaptation to the visual characteristics of the target domain, relying on the generation of target-style source samples for task-specific training. We further investigate the integration of post-HTR correction to complement visual adaptation with language adaptation, relying on large language models, which we introduce as DRAL-HTR. The proposed framework is evaluated across seven HTR datasets spanning four languages, using a single set of hyperparameters for all source-target combinations. The recognition model achieves state-of-the-art performance on four datasets and competitive results on the remaining three. In addition, the proposed DRA-HTR establishes a new state-of-the-art for domain adaptation across all seven datasets and substantially improves overall robustness and training stability compared to the original DRANet framework: it reduces the Character Error Rate (CER) in average by 13.52 percentage points, and the average standard deviation decreases from 7.23 to 1.11 percentage points. Finally, post-HTR correction further reduces the CER by 2.16 percentage points. Code is available at https://github.com/FIorentI/DRA-HTR-Disentangling-Representation-and-Adaptation-for-Handwritten-Text-Recognition.

articles.title: Fine-Tuning Fixes Mode Collapse and Over-Dispersion in LLMs
articles.summary: Recent work by Doshi and Hauser (2024), Bisbee et al. (2024), and Xie et al. (2026) raises concerns that outputs from large language models (LLMs) tend to be under-diverse: they repeat or resemble one another more often than responses from the population they are meant to represent, a phenomenon known as mode collapse. In this work, we show that whether mode-collapse, or its opposite, occurs depends on the specific model and dataset used. Further, with sufficient supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data, LLM output diversity converges toward that of the target distribution from which fine-tuning data are sampled. To quantify this comparison, we measure the probability that two responses sampled independently from the same fixed prompt coincide (collide), or their expected similarity under a kernel. We derive a bias-variance decomposition of the expected gap between the model's and target's collision probabilities, showing that SFT is not inherently biased toward mode collapse or its opposite: finite-sample SFT can leave a model either under- or over-dispersed, depending on the model and dataset. Finally, we show that the absolute gap is bounded by the square root of the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence from the target distribution to the model. Consequently, a model sufficiently close to optimal under population cross-entropy cannot exhibit arbitrarily miscalibrated diversity. We test the decomposition and the bound in three experiments: small transformers on synthetic languages, four LLMs fine-tuned on human surveys, and these LLMs fine-tuned on CodeNet, a dataset of human code solutions. More target data moves model diversity toward the human (or synthetic target) level in all experiments, consistent with our theoretical predictions. These results show that diversity miscalibration can arise from finite-sample error and shrink as SFT better approximates the target distribution.

articles.title: Grounding Language Models in Speech Does Not Fix "AI Flavor": Calibrated LLM Judges, Goodhart Traps, and a Preference-Tuning Fix
articles.summary: Chinese outputs of large language models carry a perceptible "AI flavor": formulaic sentence frames, stacked written-register connectives, repetition loops, and layout leakage. A popular hypothesis blames text-only training for the missing inner-speech layer of human writing; injecting speech or prosody signals should therefore reduce it. We test it with controlled interventions on a 0.6B model; all three fail: (i) phoneme-interleaved continued pretraining yields no spokenness gain under text-matched controls while raising repetition (+0.13 [+0.03, +0.23]); (ii) prosody-plan conditional generation reaches an adherence of only 0.257 against a pre-registered 0.50 gate; (iii) a rule-based reward built on TTS prosody-feature distance is not distinguishable in double-blind evaluation by either humans (8/16) or a calibrated LLM judge (9/16). A root cause is evaluation: single-rater blind evaluation at n~20 only detects extreme (>=85%) preferences. We therefore build a calibrated LLM-judge protocol: the judge passes catch trials on known-answer pairs (16/16; pilots 22/24 and 24/24, versus 0.75 for the human rater), then annotates with two independent judges under A/B swap, disagreement counted as a tie. Using the judge's agree labels directly as DPO pairs (no reward model), we obtain the first positive result: held-out blind win rate 0.833 (tie=0.5; bootstrap CI [0.708, 0.938]; hard-agree 0.900 [0.699, 0.972]), repetition 0.114 to 0.000, MMLU within noise. We further identify a Goodhart channel: the judge's length preference transduces into output-length collapse via pairwise DPO (median 75 chars vs a 300-char prompt); an SFT-anchor repairs it (w is a style knob: w=0.1 preserves gains). Scaling preference data from 89 to 240 pairs yields no additional judge-visible gain. We release RA-Eval v0.1: a three-layer Chinese AI-flavor evaluation framework with 382 judge-annotated preference pairs.

articles.title: MG-EDA: Maturity-Gated Skew-Normal Estimation of Distribution Algorithms
articles.summary: Gaussian estimation of distribution algorithms shrink their variance on slopes and stall far from the optimum. This paper equips the corrections that act along the direction of movement -- a mean shift, an elongation of the covariance along the path and a skewness -- with the rule they lack: a calibrated gate, driven by a maturity statistic of the population, decides whether, how strongly and for how long each correction acts, and when the gate is closed the algorithm is exactly the estimation of multivariate normal algorithm (EMNA). The statistic is a cumulative path of whitened mean shifts with an inverse-Wishart correction, whose expectation is one under a null model without systematic movement and whose quantiles give thresholds with known false-alarm rate. It gates the three corrections as three rank-one terms of one matrix sampling equation, the skewness being carried by a skew-normal sampler that preserves the estimated mean and covariance; all vanish at maturity. We call the resulting algorithm the maturity-gated EDA (MG-EDA). A full factorial study on a training set of black-box optimization benchmarking (BBOB) functions separates the parameters: variance scaling is the prerequisite, the mean shift needs a feedback correction removing the injected shift from the statistic, the elongation turns the variance loss on a slope into a gain, and the skewness substitutes for the mean shift rather than complementing it. On held-out instances MG-EDA with the first- and second-order corrections is significantly better than the skewness-only predecessor and than EMNA with variance scaling, ties with EMNA with anticipated mean shift, and trails the adapted maximum-likelihood Gaussian model (AMaLGaM) in 20 dimensions.

articles.title: RefDecoder: Enhancing Visual Generation with Conditional Video Decoding
articles.summary: Video generation powers a vast array of downstream applications. However, while the de facto standard, i.e., latent diffusion models, typically employ heavily conditioned denoising networks, their decoders often remain unconditional. We observe that this architectural asymmetry leads to significant loss of detail and inconsistency relative to the input image. To address this, we argue that the decoder requires equal conditioning to preserve structural integrity. We introduce RefDecoder, a reference-conditioned video VAE decoder by injecting high-fidelity reference image signal directly into the decoding process via reference attention. Specifically, a lightweight image encoder maps the reference frame into the detail-rich high-dimensional tokens, which are co-processed with the denoised video latent tokens at each decoder up-sampling stage. We demonstrate consistent improvements across several distinct decoder backbones (e.g., Wan 2.1 and VideoVAE+), achieving up to +2.1 dB PSNR over the unconditional baselines on the Inter4K, WebVid, and Large Motion reconstruction benchmarks. Notably, RefDecoder can be directly swapped into existing video generation systems without additional fine-tuning, and we report across-the-board improvements in subject consistency, background consistency, and overall quality scores on the VBench I2V benchmark. Beyond I2V, RefDecoder generalizes well to a wide range of visual generation tasks such as style transfer and video editing refinement.

articles.title: Average Causal Effect Estimation in DAGs with Hidden Variables: Beyond Back-Door and Front-Door Criteria
articles.summary: The identification theory for causal effects in directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) with hidden variables is well established, but methods for estimation and inference beyond the g-formula remain less developed. Previous studies have introduced influence-function-based estimators for broad classes of identifiable effects. When implemented through the observed-data density factorization, these estimators can require conditional density estimation and numerical integration, which can be statistically challenging and computationally demanding for continuous or multivariate variables. Prior work on related causal functionals has used sequential regressions and Bayes-rule representations of density ratios to avoid these requirements. Building on established identification and influence-function results, we make these reparameterizations explicit for effects identified under treatment primal fixability, Tian and Pearl's necessary and sufficient condition for identification of post-intervention law, encompassing settings beyond classical back-door and front-door identification. We construct one-step estimators under alternative nuisance parameterizations and characterize how these choices affect robustness properties and nuisance-specific L2(P) product-rate conditions for asymptotic linearity and root-n consistency. The estimators accommodate data-adaptive machine learning for nuisance estimation. To address potential violations of the target parameter bounds by one-step estimators, we also develop targeted minimum loss-based estimators (TMLEs) that respect these bounds. Our robustness characterizations and sufficient rate conditions apply to both the one-step estimators and TMLEs. Building on prior efficiency theory for hidden-variable DAGs, we further develop modifications of our estimators that exploit ordinary independence restrictions. Implementations are provided in the R flexCausal package.

articles.title: AECSF: Adaptive Ensemble Conditional Score Filtering for High-Dimensional Nonlinear Data Assimilation
articles.summary: In high-dimensional filters, particle weights can concentrate on a few members, while Gaussian updates can miss non-Gaussian posterior structure. A diffusion filter updates a forecast ensemble by gradually denoising particles in light of a new observation. Each noisy particle can correspond to several system states, and these states can have very different likelihoods. A score correction based on a single state can therefore misrepresent the posterior. We propose the Adaptive Ensemble Conditional Score Filter (AECSF), which uses the conditional Tweedie identity to express the required score through the mean state given the particle and the observation. All reverse particles share a set of proposals, but each assigns its own weights to estimate its conditional mean. As denoising proceeds, the reverse particles guide which proposals are resampled. We characterize when fixed proposals yield the exact noisy posterior score and bound the contribution of conditional-mean errors to the final sampling error. In controlled Gaussian experiments, AECSF samples the posterior more accurately than the tested likelihood-guidance rules. With 20 forecast members in 10,000-dimensional Lorenz-96, AECSF has lower RMSE and CRPS than the tested tempered SMC and kernel-density filters. On Kuramoto-Sivashinsky, the analysis ensembles also improve subsequent forecasts over the tested baselines at comparable cost. For Navier-Stokes flow, we learn a forecast prior that captures spatial dependence in vorticity and use it to reconstruct the full field from sparse velocity measurements.

articles.title: Can an LLM Repair a Language Model in Weight Space Without Gradient Training?
articles.summary: Although an external language model can select and test repairs to another model's weights, behavior can also be recovered through fixed numerical edits. We assessed the value of interactive selection in a controlled study of Transformer repair. After inspecting predictions, activation summaries, and weight statistics, the editor selects projection recipes to apply to the target without gradient updates. We analyzed 20 recorded sessions involving five masked and causal language models, comparing the selected edits with fixed projections, scripted and matched-budget black-box search, and low-rank adaptation. Under the core two-layer fault, live selection matches black-box search on SmolLM2 and Qwen2.5. For Pythia, live selection achieves 65.62% completion accuracy, compared with 0% for black-box search and 66.15% for a fixed projection. Under a separate compound fault affecting attention and feed-forward weights, both scripted and LLM-guided selection increase the descriptive five-checkpoint mean from 24.89% to 71.25% using the same operator family. On unmodified checkpoints, scripted projection yields small gains or losses on a separate set of framed questions. The experiments identify cases in which feedback changes an edit decision, operator coverage accounts for recovery, or supervised adaptation performs better. Combined with measurements of parameter restoration and preservation, these comparisons establish the scope of controller-guided repair for the tested faults and completion tasks.

articles.title: Decision-Dependent Stochastic Optimization: The Role of Distribution Dynamics
articles.summary: Distribution shifts have long been regarded as troublesome external forces that a decision-maker should either counteract or conform to. An intriguing feedback phenomenon termed decision dependence arises when the deployed decision affects the environment and alters the data-generating distribution. In the realm of performative prediction, this is encoded by distribution maps parameterized by decisions due to strategic behaviors. In contrast, we formalize an endogenous distribution shift as a feedback process featuring nonlinear dynamics that couple the evolving distribution with the decision. Stochastic optimization in this dynamic regime provides fertile ground to examine the various roles played by dynamics in the composite problem structure. To this end, we develop an online decision-making algorithm that both adapts to and shapes the dynamic distribution. Throughout the paper, we adopt a distributional perspective and demonstrate how this view facilitates characterizations of distribution dynamics and the optimality and generalization performance of the proposed algorithm. We showcase the theoretical results in an opinion dynamics context, where an opportunistic party maximizes the affinity of a population with evolving, polarized opinions, and in a recommender system scenario, featuring performance optimization with discrete distributions in the probability simplex.

articles.title: PCRG: Training-Free Pruning and Caching of Reference Tokens for Video Generation
articles.summary: Reference-to-video diffusion transformers pack the variational autoencoder (VAE) latents of all references and the generated tokens into one full-attention sequence, in which reference tokens make up about half. Because attention cost grows quadratically with sequence length, these tokens take up an even larger share of the attention computation, yet most of them are static, smooth or irrelevant to the output. To accelerate reference-conditioned generation, we propose pruning and caching of reference tokens for video generation (PCRG), a training-free, plug-and-play method that uses two signals the model already computes to assign each reference token to one of three tiers, namely pruned, cached or kept. The first is a low-level redundancy r from VAE latents, since a token whose latent barely changes over time or across its neighbors adds little new content. The second is a high-level importance g from the vision-language-model (VLM) conditioner, where the attention that the prompt and any first or last frames pay to a token tells whether the output needs to read it. Tokens that are not redundant are kept, and redundant tokens are cached if important and pruned otherwise. Pruned tokens leave the sequence before the first step with all rotary position embedding positions unchanged. Cached tokens have their keys and values computed once and reused, and kept tokens are processed as usual. On MiniMax-H3, already distilled to 8 timesteps and quantized to int8, PCRG is 1.57x faster end to end on our V2V-Bench and 1.49x faster on the public VACE-Benchmark, while the quality of VBench drops by only 0.24% and 0.17%, respectively. PCRG shortens the sequence rather than changing how attention is computed or which steps are run, so it also stacks on step caching and sparse attention. On V2V-Bench it reaches 1.86x with TeaCache, 1.82x with Spark at nearly unchanged fidelity and 2.15x with Veda.

articles.title: Raysemble: Metric 3D Bone Reconstruction from a Single X-ray
articles.summary: Raysemble reconstructs eight lumbar and pelvic bones from a single X-ray by separating shape and placement. Each 3D query samples regional and global features at its image projection. A shared decoder predicts normalized bone shapes. Predicted depth and camera geometry determine 3D centers and scales for resampling these shapes onto a common grid in millimeters. Evaluation uses 23 held-out patients with 43 CT scans, each generating one simulated anteroposterior radiograph. Without rigid alignment to CT,Raysemble leads 15 evaluated methods, averaging 65.24% Dice, 9.09 mm HD95, and 3.32 mm ASSD over three random seeds. With identical inputs, it improves Dice over VolumeNeRF by 5.86 percentage points.

articles.title: ScopeAct: Scoping Decision Models for Reliable Multi-Step Execution in Mobile GUI Agents
articles.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) enable mobile GUI agents to execute complex tasks, but frequent VLM invocations incur substantial latency and API costs. Prior work mitigates this overhead by delegating low-level action selection to lightweight decision models that choose among executable candidates. However, candidate selection alone lacks the task-level control needed to prevent premature termination and recover from failures, while candidates derived from accessibility trees (AXTrees) may not cover all actions required for task completion. To address these challenges, we introduce ScopeAct. This training-free mobile GUI agent framework combines frequent action selection with sparse VLM reasoning through the Delegation Contract and the Candidate Actions Builder. For task-level control, the Delegation Contract enables the VLM to plan subgoals with explicit completion criteria, recover from failures, and verify task completion. The decision model repeatedly selects actions to execute each subgoal without per-step VLM intervention, returning control to the VLM when execution stalls or final verification is required. For broader action coverage, the Candidate Actions Builder supplements AXTree-derived and system actions with VLM-provided text bindings for task-specific text entry and coordinates for widget-free interactions. Experiments on AndroidWorld demonstrate that ScopeAct achieves 1.7-4.8$\times$ faster execution and 3.7-8.3$\times$ lower API costs than six API-based baselines. ScopeAct requires only 5.3 and 4.6 VLM calls per task under the extended and official evaluation settings, respectively. Under the same settings, it attains 96.3% and 81.0% task success rates, surpassing the strongest baselines by 3.4 and 1.7 percentage points, respectively.

articles.title: Co-Design Gym: A Unified Benchmark for Embodiment-Policy Co-optimization
articles.summary: Finding an optimal behaviour policy within a given environment is a widely studied problem in domains as diverse as games, robotics, energy infrastructure, communication networks, and multi-agent systems. Numerous benchmarks have been developed to support such research, but the vast majority assume that the agent's embodiment (design) is fixed, focusing instead on policy learning alone. Lifting this assumption gives rise to a broader class of problems in which optimizing embodiment and policy separately is highly suboptimal. An agent's embodiment strongly shapes which control policies can be discovered, while the optimal embodiment is in turn defined by the policies it admits. To help the research community study this class of problems explicitly and systematically, we introduce Co-Design Gym - a suite of benchmark environments for jointly optimizing embodiment and policy. Our environments span domains such as robotic manipulation and locomotion, multi-robot cooperation, deformable and soft dynamics, video games, electricity grids, wireless networks, F1 racing, multi-agent warehouses, and optimal control, offering 20 environment families (domains), with over 85 distinct co-design presets in total. We further contribute a systematic evaluation of representative co-design algorithms, characterizing the current state of the art. Together, these contributions lay the groundwork for cumulative, comparable progress in co-design.

articles.title: Self-Supervised Learning for Robust Resonance Mass Regression in Cascade Decays
articles.summary: Reconstructing the mass of a heavy resonance from its decay products with missing energy is one of the central tasks that directly determine the sensitivity in new physics searches at collider experiments. Supervised learning approaches to this problem often struggle to generalize well due to the presence of various systematic uncertainties and distribution shifts. Exhausting all possible variations in the labeled data can be very compute-intensive, while a failure of the model to generalize can corrupt the reconstructed resonance widths that are critical in peak-hunting analyses. In this work, following the foundation model paradigm, we use a self-supervised approach to pre-train a transformer encoder with VICReg to learn an embedding invariant to various corruptions, then fine-tune it for mass regression on a heavy resonance with masses ranging from 2.5 to 6.5 TeV and a SUSY-like cascade decay into an eleven-body final state. We show that the pre-trained model reconstructs sharper resonance peaks and has a more stable performance under various realistic corruptions, compared to a supervised model of the same architecture trained on the same augmented data from scratch.

articles.title: FreeOcc: Decoupling Ego-Motion for Efficient 4D Occupancy Forecasting via Continuous Flow Matching
articles.summary: Current 4D occupancy world models use heavy cross-attention or deep recurrence to disentangle ego-motion from scene dynamics. This requires significant computational capacity. However, this effort is largely redundant since the ego-vehicle's intended future motion is provided by the downstream motion planner. We present FreeOcc, a lightweight continuous-time world model that introduces explicit $SE(2)$ geometric decoupling into a conditional flow-matching framework. By mathematically factoring out self-motion, we create a purely dynamic feature space. This space supports attention-free temporal fusion and allows physics-constrained ODEs to operate strictly on residual agent kinematics. To maximize deployment efficiency, FreeOcc introduces an uncertainty-aware blending mechanism. This routes well-observed voxels to a single-pass decoder, reserving the ODE solver exclusively for ambiguous, high-uncertainty regions. Requiring only 28.3M parameters-roughly 40% of comparable models-our optimal ensemble mode (FreeOcc-E) runs at 27 FPS. On nuScenes, FreeOcc achieves state-of-the-art forecasting performance with a 0.47 m Near Field Chamfer Distance (NFCD) and 32.1% mIoU. Furthermore, the model transfers zero-shot to SemanticKITTI. It also proves highly robust, retaining 92.8% of its ideal mIoU under significant sensor packet loss and timestamp jitter.

articles.title: 懂车帝回应「测试内容大调整」，称不再开放对比类内容等信息失实，具体是怎么回事？实际有哪些调整？
articles.summary: 有博主爆料称，懂车帝内部对公开测试发布了四项要求，包括不再开放对比类内容、想要发布公开测试类内容的账号必须有资质等。对此，懂车帝内容运营人员表示，此轮变化系平台严格按照《网络测评活动规范》要求，对汽车创作者在平台发布部分场景内容的规则更新。网传“内容大调整”“行业受影响”等信息多处失实，部分内容为AI撰写，未跟平台核实求证。 懂车帝回应“测试内容大调整”：信息多处失实

metrics.title: 懂车帝回应「测试内容大调整」，称不再开放对比类内容等信息失实，具体是怎么回事？实际有哪些调整？

articles.title: Generalizing Test-time Compute-optimal Scaling as an Optimizable Graph
articles.summary: Test-Time Scaling (TTS) improves large language models (LLMs) by allocating additional computation during inference, typically through parallel, sequential, or hybrid scaling. However, prior studies often assume fixed collaboration architectures (e.g., topologies) and single-model usage, overlooking that optimal architectures and model combinations can vary across tasks. Therefore, we study the novel problem of searching for compute-optimal model combinations and architectures in TTS under a fixed budget. We formalize it as a multi-LLM collaboration graph, where nodes encode roles and LLM model assignments, and edges capture information flow. This problem is challenging because (i) the combinatorial search space is prohibitively large, and (ii) task-specific requirements demand tailored designs. To address these, we reformulate the problem as probabilistic graph optimization and, through pilot experiments, derive three empirical insights into TTS collaboration graphs. Guided by these insights, we propose Agent-REINFORCE, an LLM-agent-augmented framework that mirrors the REINFORCE pipeline by mapping sampling-gradient-update to sampling-feedback-update, where feedback serves as a textual gradient to update the probabilistic graph and efficiently search for optimal multi-LLM collaboration graphs. Experiments show that Agent-REINFORCE outperforms both traditional and LLM-based baselines in sample efficiency and search performance, and effectively identifies optimal graphs under joint objectives of accuracy and inference latency.

articles.title: LF-GICP: Parameter-Free Degeneracy-Aware LiDAR Odometry via a Voxel-Normal Localizability Field
articles.summary: Scan-to-map LiDAR odometry drifts unboundedly along the unobservable axes of geometrically degenerate environments like tunnels and corridors, and existing degeneracy handling requires environment-specific parameter tuning. This paper presents a parameter-free approach. We show that in voxelized GICP the Gauss--Newton (GN) Hessian masks translational degeneracy, because covariance regularization keeps the translation block artificially well-conditioned. We bypass this with a regularization-free voxel-normal localizability field and two of its statistics: a normalized fraction $f_0$ detecting directional anisotropy, and an absolute per-voxel mass $\lambda_0$ distinguishing information absence (tunnels) from dilution (dense open scenes). A temporal-median gate combines both to trigger Fisher-information correspondence weighting. Calibrated once by fixed rules on two short sequences and then frozen, LF-GICP achieves the lowest KITTI relative translation error ($0.865\%$) under an identical evaluation protocol against re-run baselines, outperforms them on GEODE tunnels and MulRan, leads the HeLiPR mean, and generalizes across four sensor types without re-tuning. We further demonstrate empirically that straight, uniform tunnels remain unobservable along their axis for LiDAR-only registration.

articles.title: Neural variational Skyrmions as a topological benchmark: emergent symmetry, precision energies and KAN--MLP comparison
articles.summary: We propose the three-dimensional Skyrme model as a topological benchmark for neural variational methods and construct fully three-dimensional Skyrmions with baryon number $B=1,\ldots,4$ without imposing a symmetry ansatz, with high precision. For $B=2,3,4$, the relaxation of these Skyrmions starts from $B$ unit-charge lumps with random positions and orientations, which carry no symmetry information. The known toroidal, tetrahedral, and cubic Skyrmions nevertheless emerge spontaneously. The resulting variational energies for $B=1,\ldots,4$ lie slightly below the published reference values. The neural method highlights the high accuracy for retaining the topological charge, differing from $B$ by at most $10^{-6}$ in the highest-precision solutions. Our numerical method goes through physical constraint tests such as the Derrick virial relation and the Faddeev--Bogomolny bound, together with evaluation / verification through independent quadratures and resolution sweeps. We then compare Kolmogorov--Arnold networks (KANs) with multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) in more than a thousand training runs, both with and without a rational-map ansatz. With default settings, KANs appear markedly superior, but most of the gap disappears once the MLP activation function and learning rate are tuned. KANs remain more parameter-efficient and more robust at fixed epoch budget, while MLPs with the tuned activation function perform at least as well at fixed wall-clock time. We also argue that continuous gradient descent cannot smoothly change the topological sector of our neural field, clarifying the origin of topological freezing observed in our neural variational solvers. Our results on the neural methods applied to Skyrmions pave a research ground for AI-agentic benchmarks for classical topological solitons, toward AI-assisted soliton physics.

articles.title: AutoDFT: A Closed-Loop Multi-Agent Framework for Autonomous DFT Calculations
articles.summary: Density functional theory (DFT) serves as the basis for computational discovery in materials science and chemistry, yet each calculation demands extensive human effort: adjusting algorithms when convergence stalls, revising plans when unexpected physics emerges, and inserting steps as intermediate results reshape the problem. Existing LLM-based agents automate only the initial planning stage, producing a full execution plan upfront and leaving all subsequent adaptation to hand-crafted rules. As a result, these workflows remain fragile, do not generalize well beyond pre-planned scenarios, and often require expert intervention when failures or unexpected intermediate results require changes to the calculation path. Here, we introduce AutoDFT, a closed-loop multi-agent framework that embeds LLM reasoning into every stage of the DFT lifecycle, where a strategic planner produces a skeletal plan of step objectives; a step planner generates numerical parameters just in time from preceding results; and a monitor-recover-reflect cycle diagnoses failures, repairs them, and revises the plan when the evidence justifies it. We demonstrate both breadth and depth: breadth on VASPBench, a purpose-built benchmark spanning 34 tasks and 9 DFT calculation types, where AutoDFT achieves 94.1% task-level success with GPT-5.2; and depth on established materials databases, where AutoDFT produces quantitatively reliable property predictions across electronic, magnetic, and energetic properties. By closing the loop between planning and execution, AutoDFT enables experimentalists without deep computational expertise to obtain reliable first-principles results. Our code is available at https://github.com/penghui-yang/AutoDFT.

articles.title: Carry the Fine Print: Budget-Aware Visual Token Compression for Document OCR
articles.summary: Visual token compression often treats salience or similarity as a proxy for transcription importance. Complete document OCR breaks this assumption: small symbols and repeated entries can be indispensable to the transcript despite being visually inconspicuous. We present Select and Compensate, a two-stage framework built on a simple idea: choosing where to retain a token need not determine all the evidence it carries. Selection combines adaptive encoding resolution with global importance and local contrast to choose which tokens to retain as anchors. Compensation enriches these anchors with nearby discarded content and its relative position, without adding tokens. The OCR backbone remains frozen, and native coordinates and structural tokens are preserved. We evaluate complete page transcription across five backbones on OmniDocBench and document reconstruction on MPDocBench. With half the original visual tokens, our input-adapted configuration reaches 95.42 OmniDocBench Overall on Ovis versus 96.09 for the uncompressed model, and paired evaluations show gains over simply reducing the input resolution on both benchmarks. With the original input grid, our method stays within 0.17 points of the uncompressed model at 75% retention and exceeds a learned global selector by 4.70 points at 25%. On a fixed 200-page Ovis workload at the same 50% visual-token budget, only 3 of its outputs hit the length limit, versus 30-34 for the evaluated RTPrune, DivPrune, and HiPrune adaptations, and it finishes the batch 35-40% sooner. Code will be made publicly available.

articles.title: LoopNav: Benchmarking Spatial Consistency in World Models
articles.summary: The ability to simulate the world in a spatially consistent manner is a crucial requirement for effective world models. Such a model enables high-quality visual generation, and also ensures the reliability of world models for downstream tasks such as simulation and planning. It must not only retain long-horizon observational information, but also enables the construction of explicit or implicit internal spatial representations. However, existing datasets do not explicitly enforce spatial consistency constraints, limiting both the ability to systematically evaluate this capability and to learn it through data-driven approaches. Furthermore, most existing benchmarks primarily emphasize visual coherence or generation quality, neglecting the requirement of long-range spatial consistency. To bridge this gap, we propose LoopNav, a dataset and corresponding benchmark centered on loop-based navigation for evaluating spatial consistency. The dataset comprises 200 hours of loop-based navigation videos with actions, collected from diverse locations in the open-world environment of Minecraft. We further introduce a Scene Graph Consistency Score(SGCS) to quantify spatial consistency while remaining invariant to pixel-level variations. Dataset, benchmark, and code are open-sourced to support future research.

articles.title: Adaptive Determinantal Client Scheduling in Federated Learning
articles.summary: Scheduling clients for model training is critical in federated learning due to both data and system heterogeneity. Most previous works focus on the quality of the scheduled clients to achieve faster convergence, shorter wall-clock convergence time, or better average model performance. They rarely consider the diversity of clients, which is important to counter heterogeneity and improve performance for the worst-off clients. In this work, we advocate the use of determinantal point processes (DPPs) to model and enhance the diversity in client scheduling. We first design the kernel matrices of DPPs using gradient information and quality scores, which inherently enables a flexible quality-diversity trade-off. Applying fast MAP inference over DPPs, we propose Adaptive Determinantal Client Scheduling (ADCS) in FL. We further quantify the gradient approximation error of ADCS and develop convergence analysis for general biased client selection in FL with non-convex loss functions. We conduct comparative numerical experiments showing that ADCS outperforms state-of-the-art client scheduling algorithms, including both quality-based and diversity-based ones.

articles.title: On the Identifiability of Regime-Switching Models with Multi-Lag Dependencies
articles.summary: Identifiability is central to the interpretability of deep latent variable models, ensuring parameterisations are uniquely determined by the data-generating distribution. However, it remains underexplored for deep regime-switching time series. We develop a general theoretical framework for multi-lag Regime-Switching Models (RSMs), encompassing Markov Switching Models (MSMs) and Switching Dynamical Systems (SDSs). For MSMs, we formulate the model as a temporally structured finite mixture and prove identifiability of both the number of regimes and the multi-lag transitions in a nonlinear-Gaussian setting. For SDSs, we establish identifiability of the latent variables up to permutation and scaling via temporal structure, which in turn yields conditions for identifiability of regime-dependent latent causal graphs (up to regime/node permutations). Our results hold in a fully unsupervised setting through architectural and noise assumptions that are directly enforceable via neural network design. We complement the theory with a flexible variational estimator that satisfies the assumptions and validate the results on synthetic benchmarks. Across real-world data sets from neuroscience, finance, and climate, identifiability leads to more trustworthy interpretability analysis, which is crucial for scientific discovery.

articles.title: Bringing AI Assistance to the Beznau Nuclear Power Plant: A Hierarchical System of LLM Agents for Reactor Monitoring
articles.summary: Beznau Unit 1 in Switzerland, in operation since 1969, is the most experienced nuclear reactor still running worldwide. Five decades of incremental modernization have left its monitoring systems, alarm logs, variable catalogs, technical specifications and investigation reports in separate silos that were never designed to be queried together. As a result, investigating a core instrumentation anomaly means slow, manual gathering of knowledge scattered across databases, documents, and experienced colleagues. We present a hierarchical multi-agent assistant built on large language models (LLMs) to support these investigations and reduce the need for tedious manual searches in SAP systems. An orchestrating agent breaks down an engineer's question and hands the parts to specialized sub-agents, each with read-only access to one source. Domain expertise is written as natural-language procedures that plant engineers can read, review and revise. The system is strictly advisory, with every answer traced back to its sources. We also report organizational lessons from introducing agentic AI into a culture built on safety, traceability and conservative change. Beyond the technical architecture, the Beznau case study examines how an assistant can be introduced into a setting where evidence must be traceable, changes carefully reviewed, and operational decisions retained by plant personnel, paving the way for the responsible use of agentic AI in industrial plant monitoring.

articles.title: A Scale-Adaptive Framework for Joint Spatiotemporal Super-Resolution with Diffusion Models
articles.summary: Deep-learning video super-resolution has progressed rapidly, but climate applications typically super-resolve (increase resolution) either space or time, and joint spatiotemporal models are often designed for a single pair of super-resolution (SR) factors (upscaling spatial and temporal ratio between the low-resolution sequence and the high-resolution sequence), limiting transfer across spatial resolutions and temporal cadences (frame rates). We present a scale-adaptive framework that reuses the same architecture across factors by decomposing spatiotemporal SR into a deterministic prediction of the conditional mean, with attention, and a residual conditional diffusion model, with an optional mass-conservation (same precipitation amount in inputs and outputs) transform to preserve aggregated totals. Assuming that larger SR factors primarily increase underdetermination (hence required context and residual uncertainty) rather than changing the conditional-mean structure, scale adaptivity is achieved by retuning three factor-dependent hyperparameters before retraining: the diffusion noise schedule amplitude beta (larger for larger factors to increase diversity), the temporal context length L (set to maintain comparable attention horizons across cadences) and optionally a third, the mass-conservation function f (tapered to limit the amplification of extremes for large factors). Demonstrated on reanalysis precipitation over France (Comephore), the same architecture spans super-resolution factors from 1 to 25 in space and 1 to 6 in time, yielding a reusable architecture and tuning recipe for joint spatiotemporal super-resolution across scales.

articles.title: Idempotency Is Not Recovery: A Fault-Injection Study of Language-Model Agent Tool Actions
articles.summary: When a language-model agent's tool call is interrupted, the action may already have changed an external system without confirmation. Retrying risks duplication; assuming success may conceal an action that never occurred. We study these failure modes in a controlled agent runtime combining authorization, an action ledger, target-side idempotency, reconciliation, and evidence sealing. We inject ten single-host fault classes and compare four configurations and three ablations using a target-side oracle separate from the runtime ledger. On each of Windows and Linux, 7,513 trials used 96 captured model responses from 24 constructed cases. In 200 known original crash and replay pairs, the full configuration recorded 0/200 repeated effects versus 117/200 for each simpler baseline. A ledger-related ablation had 170/170 orphaned effects versus 0/170 and 200/300 recovery successes versus 300/300 for the full configuration. Disabling reconciliation left 100/100 known post-effect crash outcomes ambiguous despite no observed duplicates. A separate supplement designed after the initial results and reusing the same inputs found a similar pattern under response loss or delay. The full runtime had about one-seventh of fail-open throughput, while injected evidence-write faults left 75/100 trials per platform unresolved. These findings distinguish duplicate suppression from recovery and identify their measured reliability and performance tradeoffs within the tested benchmark.

articles.title: A Two-Parameter Weibull Framework for Diagnosing Transformer Weight Distributions
articles.summary: Transformer checkpoints contain billions of weights, yet how their element-wise distributions vary across components, models, and training is hard to characterize. We fit the magnitude distribution of each analyzed weight matrix with a two-parameter Weibull reference model under a fixed middle-80% protocol. For i.i.d. Gaussian initialization, the corresponding half-Normal target has protocol-fitted shape $k_0 \approx 1.20$. Matched comparisons with gamma and lognormal favor Weibull for most component groups; support is less decisive for separately stored MHA query/key projections, and no tested single family cleanly describes matrices carrying a secondary weight population. Across 12 model entries spanning seven families, terminal FFN shape medians fall in a narrow band, $k \in [1.186, 1.204]$ (CV $= 0.51\%$), whereas query/key projections show architecture-associated departures. This stability is macroscopic only: in the five Pythia models whose released step-0 checkpoints permit a paired comparison, FFN and attention-output matrices remain near the reference shape despite large displacement and reorientation, so terminal shape similarity is not explained by parameter proximity alone. The fitted shape $k$ is read as a reference-relative central-body shape indicator and the scale $\lambda$ as a magnitude coordinate; neither is presented as a predictor of downstream performance. In a Qwen case study, the screen localizes a shallow-FFN secondary small-magnitude population, and direct raw-weight analysis of a flagged block traces much of that population to coherently suppressed intermediate channels. The method requires only released checkpoints and complements behavioral and structural analyses. The code and reference database are available at https://github.com/tiexinding/NPM-Weibull-public.

articles.title: Convergence Rate of the Last Iterate of Stochastic Proximal Algorithms
articles.summary: We analyze two classical algorithms for solving additively composite convex optimization problems where the objective is the sum of a smooth term and a nonsmooth regularizer. The first algorithm is the proximal stochastic gradient method for a single regularizer; the second is the randomized incremental proximal method, which uses the proximal operator of a randomly selected function when the regularizer is given as the sum of many nonsmooth functions. We focus on relaxing the bounded variance assumption that is common, yet stringent, for getting last iterate convergence rates. We prove the $\widetilde{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$ rate of convergence for the last iterate of both algorithms under componentwise convexity and smoothness, which is optimal up to log terms. Our results apply directly to graph-guided regularizers that arise in multi-task and federated learning, where the regularizer decomposes as a sum over edges of a collaboration graph.

articles.title: Empathetic Motion Generation for Humanoid Educational Robots via Reasoning-Guided Vision--Language--Motion Diffusion Architecture
articles.summary: This article suggests a reasoning-guided vision-language-motion diffusion framework (RG-VLMD) for generating instruction-aware co-speech gestures for humanoid robots in educational scenarios. The system integrates multi-modal affective estimation, pedagogical reasoning, and teaching-act-conditioned motion synthesis to enable adaptive and semantically consistent robot behavior. A gated mixture-of-experts model predicts Valence/Arousal from input text, visual, and acoustic features, which then mapped to discrete teaching-act categories through an affect-driven policy.These signals condition a diffusion-based motion generator using clip-level intent and frame-level instructional schedules via additive latent restriction with auxiliary action-group supervision. Compared to a baseline diffusion model, our proposed method produces more structured and distinctive motion patterns, as verified by motion statics and pairwise distance analysis. Generated motion sequences remain physically plausible and can be retargeted to a NAO robot for real-time execution. The results reveal that reasoning-guided instructional conditioning improves gesture controllability and pedagogical expressiveness in educational human-robot interaction.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal Landslide Runout Reconstruction from Sparse Observations with LAPIS-SHRED
articles.summary: Reconstructing the spatiotemporal evolution of landslide runout from limited observations is a central challenge in geohazard assessment: transient flow dynamics are rarely observed directly, and available data are often confined to post-event deposits or brief monitoring windows. We apply LAPIS-SHRED (LAtent Phase Inference from Short time sequence using SHallow REcurrent Decoders) to reconstruct runout events near Mount St. Helens, USA. Trained on physics-based simulation ensembles, the framework supports both backward reconstruction from single frame and forward prediction from short initial window across different runout regimes. Using 32 sensor observations from a single timepoint, LAPIS-SHRED recovers complete runout trajectories with NRMSE below 5.8%, robust across varying observational and training conditions. Validation against observed deposits yields spatial correlation of r = 0.843 against the calibrated simulator's r = 0.853. These results suggest that latent-space temporal inference offers a viable pathway for spatiotemporal landslide reconstruction under extreme observational constraints typical of field settings.

articles.title: Practical insights into controlling exponential concentration in quantum machine learning
articles.summary: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models are often limited by exponential concentration, where quantum observables become insensitive to input variations as system size increases.
